overview.description: Dudák (Czech for 'Bagpiper') is a popular Czech shedding game closely related to the Russian game Durak. Played with a 32ndcard Germanndsuited deck, the game is a contest of attrition where players must defend against 'attacks' by beating cards with higher ranks or trumps. The goal is to empty one's hand; the last player left holding cards is the loser—the Dudák.

history.origins: Dudák evolved as a regional variant of the Russian Durak, adapted for the 32ndcard deck prevalent in Bohemia and Moravia.
timeline: 18thnd19th Century: Shedding games spread across Eastern and Central Europe.
1900s: Dudák becomes a standard tavern game in the Czech Republic.
Modern: Maintained as a simple social game for all ages.
history.evolution: Features a unique 'Secret Dudák' variant where trumps are not known until a player reveals them.
history.cultural: The loser being called a 'Bagpiper' is a lighthearted insult typical of Czech social gaming.

setup.deck: 32ndcard Germanndsuited pack: Acorns (žaludy), Leaves (zelené), Hearts (červené), Balls (kule).
setup.dealing: Usually 4nd6 cards to each player (common variation handles all 32 cards being dealt).

rules.objective: Be the first to shed all cards. Avoid being the last player left with cards.
rules.gameplay:
1. Attacking: One player leads a card (the attack).
2. Defending: The defender must play a higher card of the same suit or a trump.
3. Beating cards: If a defender beats all attacking cards, the cards are discarded (Vejbit).
4. Failure: If a defender cannot beat a card, they must pick up common pile.
keyRules: Hearts are often the permanent trump suit.
Attacking cards must match the rank of any card currently on the table to continue an attack.
In 'Secret Dudák,' trumps are revealed midndhand by the first player who chooses to do so.

strategy.basic: Save your trumps for late in the game to avoid picking up a large pile of cards when the deck is empty.
strategy.intermediate: Teamwork: If you are the attacker, lead ranks that your partner (another attacker) can follow up with, to overwhelm the defender.
strategy.advanced: Card Counting: Essential in a 32ndcard deck. Know which Queens (Overs) and Kings have been discarded to gauge when your 10s or 9s become safe beats.
tips: Avoid 'dirtying' your hand by picking up too many suit cards early.
In Secret Dudák, revealing your trump suit too early gives opponents an advantage in planning their attacks.

list.name: Open Dudák (Otevřený Dudák)
list.description: Each player's trump suit is decided in advance and known to all; rules after trumps declared apply throughout.
list.emptyOverridesReason: Variant documented in sources; engine overrides to be added when implementing.

list.name: Pocket Dudák (Kapsičkový Dudák)
list.description: Each player is dealt a hand plus a face-down trump card; trumps are revealed when the player declares.
list.emptyOverridesReason: Variant documented in sources; engine overrides to be added when implementing.

list.name: Secret Dudák (Tajný Dudák)
list.description: Like Pocket Dudák except no one may see others' trump cards until the owner declares and turns the card face up.
list.emptyOverridesReason: Variant documented in sources; engine overrides to be added when implementing.

list.name: Dudák with a Talon (Lízaný Dudák)
list.description: Not all cards are dealt; remainder forms a talon. Players draw to replenish hand after play; when talon is empty, play continues as standard Dudák.
list.emptyOverridesReason: Variant documented in sources; engine overrides to be added when implementing.

difficulty.easy: Wastes high trumps on low attackers; doesn't count discards.
difficulty.medium: Conserves trumps; recognizes when to take a pile to gain strategic ranks.
difficulty.hard: Perfect memory of all 'Vejbit' (discarded) cards; executes complex multi-card attacks.

considerations: AI must handle the 'Secret Trump' transition, adjusting strategy instantly when the trump suit is revealed.

engine.deckDescription: One 32-card German-suited deck: four suits (Acorns, Leaves, Hearts, Bells) with eight ranks per suit (7, 8, 9, 10, Unter, Ober, King, Ace). Used for Dudak and similar games; created by removing the 6s and lower from a full German pack. No jokers.
engine.suitDescription: Four German suits: Acorns (Eichel), Leaves (Laub), Hearts (Herz), Bells (Schellen), each with eight cards. Trump and lead rules depend on the variant; follow suit when able. Card order and point values follow the regional 32-card convention for trick-taking.
engine.rankDescription: Eight ranks per suit from low to high: 7, 8, 9, 10, Unter, Ober, King, Ace. Point values typically follow Ace-Ten scoring (Ace 11, Ten 10, King 4, Ober 3, Unter 2, numerals 0). Strength and trick order are as in standard 32-card German games.
